title: Stitchboard prefill & batching lab scrum - 2029-08-14
content:
Sprint context and goal:
- Quick sync for the stitchboard prefill experiments and the micro-batching timing anomaly observed in last week's canary. Primary goal: decide whether to revert kernel patch or patch prefill timing heuristics as a hotfix.

What happened (summary):
- 2029-08-12 evening canary: new kernel-scheduler PR landed (PR #4521) to improve kernel coalescing for long seqs.
- Observed a 2.2–3.5% P50 latency regression on seq_len 256 for the hosted route group under typical traffic. Regression shows up only when KV-prefill shadowing is enabled.
- Trace shows extra 1–2ms spent in 'prefill coordination' for ~7% of requests; these requests overlap with coalescing window boundary.
- No notable throughput drop; tail (P99.9) unaffected.

Hypothesis threads we discussed:
1) Kernel coalescing change increased time-to-first-prefill by nudging coalescer timing (race with prefill coordinator).
2) Prefill shadowing path: when cache miss + prefill in-flight + coalescer shift => extra synchronization penalty.
3) Metric instrumentation gap: our histogram bucket boundaries miss the short sync spikes, so observed regression is undercounted in some dashboards.

Immediate data we pulled / experiments run during the sync:
- Re-ran bench harness with seq_len 256, KV-shadow ON/OFF, kernel-patch ON/OFF (local lab GPUs). Results: patch-only causes 2.4% P50 up if KV-shadow ON; patch-only no regression with KV-shadow OFF.
- Flamegraphs (perf + traces) attached in PR comments.
- Canary traffic replay with QPS throttled to 60% shows same pattern; suggests not load-only effect.

Decisions and next steps (agreed):
- Short term (hotfix): revert merged kernel scheduler changes from PR #4521 on canary and prod for routes with KV-shadow enabled. Target: deploy revert by EOD 2029-08-15 if no blocking issues. (Owner: Benji)
- Medium term: implement a small change in prefill coordinator to add a non-blocking fast-path when coalescer indicates imminent dispatch. This reduces coordination syscall cost. Target: prototype + lab run by 2029-08-20. (Owner: Lin)
- Instrumentation: add explicit 100us buckets around prefill coordination waits and surface as separate metric 'prefill_coord_wait_us' in Console. Add a tracing span with recruiting tags to link kernel coalescer decisions to prefill coordinator events. (Owner: Asha)
- Canary plan: once revert is rolled to canary, run the previously-failing traffic replay and compare P50/P95 across three configs: baseline (pre-patch), patched (PR #4521), patched+prefill-fastpath (when available).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Does the coalescer timing drift only at certain host kernel versions? Need a host-level check (syscalls scheduling) — ask infra to surface host-kernel on canary fleet. (Ticket logged: INF-2903)
- How widespread is KV-shadow usage across customer routes? Risk of revert impacting other latency-sensitive routes. Product to provide list of high-risk routes. (Action: ping product-hosted-api)

Action items (who / when):
- Benji: submit and coordinate revert rollout for PR #4521 to canary (due 2029-08-15).
- Lin: prototype prefill fast-path and run lab experiments (due 2029-08-20).
- Asha: add prefill_coord_wait_us metric + tracing span; update dashboards and alert thresholds (due 2029-08-18).
- Diego: run host-kernel-version correlation sweep across canary machines and report anomalies (due 2029-08-17).
- Product (assigned via slack): provide list of top-20 customer routes using KV-shadow by 2029-08-16.

Notes from quick lab log (raw):
- bench-aug-256-run-14: with coalescer=patched + kvshadow=on: P50 12.6ms -> baseline 12.3ms. CPU sampling shows 0.9ms in coordinator lock.
- bench-aug-256-run-15: patched + kvshadow=off: P50 12.32ms -> matches baseline.
- trace snippet: span prefill_coordinator.wait (avg 700us) spikes to 1.8ms in ~6% of traces coincident with coalescer boundary ops.

Guidance for oncall if revert occurs:
- Watch prefill_coord_wait_us and token-per-second throughput for canary hosts. If we see tail blowups (P99.5 up by >10%) abort revert and call SRE.
- Keep canary window min 45 minutes with replay traffic plus 10 minutes live traffic.

Retrospective notes (for post-mortem):
- We need a gating test for kernel scheduler changes that includes KV-shadow and prefill coordinator in the loop (currently gating tests run coalescer+kernel but with KV-shadow disabled).
- Consider a small simulation harness that replays coalescer timing jitter against prefill coordinator to catch lock/race micro-regressions.

Misc / misc brainstorms captured: 
- Could we move prefill coordinator to a lock-free ring buffer and only notify coalescer via a single atomic write? Pros: less syscall contention; cons: more complex edge-case for eviction.
- Another thought: introduce a 'grace window' where coalescer avoids moving dispatch boundary for N microseconds after a prefill commit. Might be easier but could slightly increase latency when coalescer could have benefited.

Meeting attendees (live): Asha, Benji, Lin, Diego, Maya (SRE), product rep: Clara.

Slack clip summary (to paste into incident channel):
- "Canary saw a small P50 regression on seq256 tied to kernel coalescer changes when KV-shadow is on. Reverting patch to canary today; building prefill fast-path as next step. Patch PR #4521. JIRA INF-2897. See doc: Confluence Prefill Stitchboard Notes."
